Assistant

Responses are generated using AI and may contain mistakes.

Integrations let agents work with the apps your team already uses.For example, an agent can read an email from Gmail, extract data from an attachment, add a row to Google Sheets, and send a Slack update.

![Connectors page showing available integrations like Outlook, Gmail, Google Sheets, QuickBooks, and SAP](https://mintcdn.com/nanonets-fb7e8f2a/eksLpltcNl29FEi2/images/connectors.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=eksLpltcNl29FEi2&q=85&s=03d6180a883db63815098f165a7ab93e)

The Connectors page lists the apps you can connect: email, spreadsheets, storage, messaging, and business systems.

## [​](https://agents.nanonets.com/docs/guide/integrations\#what-you-can-connect)  What you can connect

Common connection types include:

- Email: Gmail and Microsoft Outlook.
- Spreadsheets and storage: Google Sheets and Google Drive.
- Messaging: Slack, Microsoft Teams, and RingCentral.
- Business systems: SAP, NetSuite, Microsoft Dynamics, Sage Intacct, and Sage X3.
- Databases: PostgreSQL.
- Healthcare and CRM systems: AdvancedMD, AthenaHealth, DrChrono, GoHighLevel, and more.
- Team tools: Linear, HubSpot, Notion, Metabase, Gong, and other connected apps.

## [​](https://agents.nanonets.com/docs/guide/integrations\#connect-an-app)  Connect an app

1

Open Connectors

Go to **Connectors** from the sidebar.

2

Choose the app

Find the app you want the agent to use.

3

Connect your account

Some apps ask you to sign in. Others ask for account details from your admin.

4

Add it to an agent

Add the related tool to your agent, such as Gmail, Google Sheets, or SAP.

![Connect to PostgreSQL pop-up window with fields for host, port, database, and username](https://mintcdn.com/nanonets-fb7e8f2a/eksLpltcNl29FEi2/images/connector-modal.png?fit=max&auto=format&n=eksLpltcNl29FEi2&q=85&s=5342fce59c8c55dd7b801b24617035c9)

A connector setup window, here for PostgreSQL, asking for connection details. Some apps use sign-in instead.

## [​](https://agents.nanonets.com/docs/guide/integrations\#connections-belong-to-a-workspace)  Connections belong to a workspace

Each connection is tied to the workspace you are using.If your company has separate workspaces for Finance and Operations, each workspace can have its own connected apps.

Check that you are in the right workspace before connecting an app. This keeps access clean and avoids using the wrong account.

## [​](https://agents.nanonets.com/docs/guide/integrations\#how-agents-use-integrations)  How agents use integrations

Connecting an app gives Nanonets permission to use it.The agent still needs the right tool added to its setup. For example:

- To send Gmail messages, connect Gmail and add the Gmail tool.
- To update Google Sheets, connect Google Sheets and add the Google Sheets tool.
- To create ERP records, connect the ERP and add the related ERP tool.

## [​](https://agents.nanonets.com/docs/guide/integrations\#use-integrations-with-triggers)  Use integrations with triggers

Integrations can also start tasks.Examples:

- Run an invoice agent when a new email arrives.
- Run a report agent on a schedule.
- Run a workflow when a connected system sends an update.

Learn more in [Set up an agent](https://agents.nanonets.com/docs/guide/build-an-agent).
